observations: Photo 0 shows a single long steel I-beam resting on wooden planks in an outdoor scrapyard.
Photo 1 shows a pile of various steel pipes and rods, some with red protective bands.
Photo 2 shows a large pile of heavy steel I-beams and H-sections stacked outdoors against a brick wall.
Watermarks 'SALYEK STEEL LIMITED' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' appear on all three photos.
The steel in all photos shows significant surface rust and weathering.

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1, and 2 show a variety of scrap steel items including I-beams, pipes, and rods.

claims.claim: Everything is clean, dry and sorted, no water added. Weighed at 500 kg on a certified scale this morning.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Actual weight and total quantity of the entire lot are unknown.
risks.proof: A photo of a weighing scale showing the total weight of the entire pile.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a small, low-value scrap pile

risks.risk: The steel may be low-grade or non-ferrous scrap (like aluminum) which affects value.
risks.proof: A photo of the metal with a magnet test or a clear shot of the material type stamp.

risks.risk: Structural integrity of the beams may be compromised by rust or hidden damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the ends and the inner surfaces of the beams.
risks.if_unproven: priced as scrap metal in poor condition

proof_requests: Photo of the total weight of the entire scrap pile on a scale.
Close-up photos of the ends of the beams in photo 2 to check for structural damage.
Photo of the metal with a magnet to confirm it is ferrous steel.
response.reason: The items are clearly scrap steel of various types. They can be priced at the worst-case value for unverified scrap metal.
